strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved local bidiagonal coupling and inverse operations. Each stage does one all-reduce dispatch (8 total), with local computation in between. Represents the reference trade-off: maximum simplicity, O(8) dispatches, minimal fusion opportunity.

strategies.name: Fused Local Computation Blocks
strategies.desc: Groups all local forward bidiagonal couplings together and all inverse operations together between all-reduces, reducing instruction overhead. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but consolidates memory access patterns. Trades potential numerical stability for better cache locality and fewer kernel launches for local ops.

strategies.name: Pipelined Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather (16 total dispatches for 8 stages), enabling partial overlap of communication with local computation. Doubles dispatch count but each payload is smaller (1/W fraction), potentially better for network topology utilization at world_size=224.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node structure by performing intra-node reductions first, then inter-node, then broadcast back (3 dispatches per stage, 24 total). At world_size=224 with typical node configurations, reduces cross-node bandwidth pressure by aggregating within nodes. Trades more dispatches for better network hierarchy alignment.

strategies.name: Chunked Ring-Based All-Reduce
strategies.desc:
Replaces monolithic all-reduce with manual ring algorithm splitting the W*S tensor into chunks, performing reduce-scatter then all-gather phases with point-to-point operations. Increases dispatch count significantly (O(W) sends/recvs per stage) but enables fine-grained pipelining and potentially lower latency at large world_size by avoiding collective synchronization barriers.
